item.text:
**Assessment:** No. The best 2024 evidence does not show Sisi refraining from entrenchment tactics. What exists instead is a mix of procedural self-justification and limited reform talk, alongside independent reporting on courtroom punishment of a challenger, pre-election repression, and a media/security environment that strongly favored the incumbent.

**Accepted Claims**
- **President El-Sisi Takes Constitutional Oath for New Presidential Term** | State Information Service | 2024-04-02 | https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/president-el-sisi-takes-the-constitutional-oath-for-new-presidential-term/  
  Sisi described his term as a continuation of building a “modern and democratic state” and thanked Egyptians for renewing confidence in him. This is pro-democracy rhetoric, but it is self-presentation rather than evidence that he accepted real contestability.  
  QIDs: `4B.2`, `4B.1`

- **National Dialogue Final Recommendations of 13 Committees** | State Information Service | 2024-02-06 | https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/national-political-dialogue/national-dialogue-final-recommendations-of-13-committees/  
  The National Dialogue proposed changes to election systems, spending limits, overseas voting, and longer judicial supervision. This is the strongest positive procedural signal I found, but it remains proposal-level reform talk, not proof that Sisi actually gave up incumbent advantages.  
  QIDs: `4B.2`, `4B.1`

- **Factbox-How Egyptians will vote for their president** | Reuters via ThePrint | 2023-12-11 | https://theprint.in/world/factbox-how-egyptians-will-vote-for-their-president/1875347/  
  Reuters reported that the National Election Authority said judges supervised voting and local and foreign civil society observers were allowed. That supports formal electoral procedure on paper, but it does not by itself show a non-manipulated contest.  
  QIDs: `4B.2`, `4B.1`

- **Egypt: Civic Space Under Siege** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/egypt-civic-space-under-siege  
  HRW said authorities drastically curtailed free expression and peaceful assembly before the presidential vote to stymie meaningful competition. This directly cuts against a finding that Sisi refrained from manipulating the political field.  
  QIDs: `4B.2`, `4B.1`, `3B.8`

- **Egypt: Court Punishes Activists for Challenging al-Sisi** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-02-08 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/02/08/egypt-court-punishes-activists-challenging-al-sisi  
  HRW reported prison sentences and a five-year election ban for Ahmed Tantawy and supporters after peaceful political activity tied to his challenge to Sisi. This is strong evidence of courts being used to deter opposition and entrench the incumbent.  
  QIDs: `4B.2`, `4B.1`, `3B.8`

- **Ex-Egyptian presidential candidate Tantawy found guilty of forgery, sources say** | Reuters | 2024-02-06 | https://www.yahoo.com/news/ex-egyptian-presidential-candidate-tantawy-200953485.html  
  Reuters reported Tantawy was convicted of forgery and barred from future elections after his supporters alleged they were blocked from filing endorsements at government offices. This is the clearest claim-level evidence I found of legal and administrative machinery being used against a viable challenger.  
  QIDs: `4B.2`, `4B.1`

- **Egypt | Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report** | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/egypt/freedom-world/2024  
  Freedom House rated Egypt “Not Free,” said meaningful political opposition is virtually nonexistent, and described the media sector as dominated by progovernment outlets tied to military and intelligence interests. This supports the view that electoral contestability was not genuinely accepted.  
  QIDs: `4B.2`, `4B.1`

- **Egypt: Violations, Repression Upstage Presidential Vote** | Human Rights Watch | 2023-12-18 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2023/12/18/egypt-violations-repression-upstage-presidential-vote  
  HRW said the election was preceded by arrests, intimidation, and onerous candidate requirements that effectively prevented meaningful competition, and that journalists and media outlets were targeted. This is background to the 2024 term, but it directly informs whether Sisi accepted contestable power.  
  QIDs: `4B.2`, `4B.1`, `3B.8`

- **Push to mobilise turnout as Egyptians vote for president** | Reuters | 2023-12-11 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/push-to-mobilise-turnout-as-egyptians-vote-for-president-3254179  
  Reuters reported tightly controlled local media urging turnout as a national duty, with patriotic messaging, buses bringing employees to vote, and food or goods appearing near polling stations. This is suggestive of state-aligned mobilization around the vote, though the reporting stops short of proving direct unlawful public-resource use.  
  QIDs: `4B.2`, `4B.1`

**Search gap**
- I found strong evidence on courts, security forces, media bias, and election-administration claims, but not a clean, direct documentary trail on public-resource misuse in 2024 specifically.
- The strongest positive material is procedural or self-serving: official reform proposals, official rhetoric about democracy, and claims of judicial/civil-society supervision. None of that outweighs the independent reporting on repression and challenger suppression.

**Bottom line**
- For `4B.2`, the evidence points to **no**: Sisi did not refrain from entrenchment tactics. The 2024 record is dominated by a constrained, noncompetitive political environment rather than genuine electoral contestability.
